stanza: the crypt under an old mountain village church, present day: a low vaulted ceiling of rough grey stone, rough stone walls with deep arched niches, a worn stone floor; in the two side niches old human skulls and long bones are stacked neatly, like in an ossuary; many white church candles stand on the floor and on the stone ledges, some burning, with long drips of wax; on the left wall, in a small niche of its own, an ancient plague doctor's mask of black cracked leather with a long beak, with a single round brass lens in place of the right eye, hangs from an iron nail above a small worn stone plaque. At the back, in the middle, a large arched niche. Low stone steps come down on the right.
persone: One figure: in the large arched niche at the back stands a woman in her sixties who has changed into something else, upright and still like the statue of a saint. Her skin has become pure white and smooth like candle wax, slightly translucent and glossy, with thick drips of wax running down from her chin, her elbows and her hands, as on a melted candle; her eyes are closed and sealed under a smooth layer of wax; her long grey hair hangs loose down to her waist; her hands are joined in prayer in front of her chest, and her fingers have fused together into one long, thin black point like a burnt candle wick; she wears a long pale blue nightgown, stiff and stained with wax. She stands perfectly straight, her sealed face turned towards the viewer as if she could see.
pose: the waxen woman standing upright in the large niche at the back, her hands joined in front of her chest
